subject: EU Data Residency & Export Controls — Next Steps
messages:
From: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acmehealth.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmehealth.eu>
Date: 2026-07-21T15:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Intro + quick security questions

Thanks for the call today, Marissa — helpful overview. A couple follow-ups from our side specific to EU deployments and export controls before we proceed to procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether Redwood offers data residency in the EU (managed region) and where customer data is stored at rest?
- Do you have a SOC 2 Type II report we can review, or a summary of your compliance posture?
- We need to initiate a vendor security questionnaire; can you send a completed copy or point-of-contact?
- Any restrictions related to OFAC/ITAR or cross-border data transfer we should be aware of?

Appreciate a short recap & next steps so procurement knows what to expect.

Best,
Alex
Senior IT Ops, Acme Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Carter <alex.carter@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-21T19:10:00Z
Subject: Re: EU Data Residency & Export Controls — Next Steps

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick recap and proposed next steps below. Attaching: SOC2 summary, EU residency factsheet, and a completed vendor security questionnaire template for your records.

Recap:
- EU Data Residency: Redwood supports a dedicated EU region (data-at-rest in eu-west-1 managed by our EU data plane). Customers can pin workloads to that region; control plane metadata is configurable depending on Private vs Hosted.
- SOC 2: We have a SOC 2 Type II report for the hosted platform (most recent audit completed Q1 2026). Full report is available under NDA — summarized PDF attached.
- GDPR & HIPAA: Our DPA and BAAs are available; we support controller/processor terms.
- Export controls: We are not an ITAR-controlled service. For OFAC, we follow standard US export restrictions; we block sanctioned entities and follow customer screening (we can provide an export controls statement).

Next steps:
1) Rafael from our security team can 1:1 with your security contact for any technical clarifications (cc'd).
2) Please have procurement review the attached questionnaire; if you prefer, send your version and we will populate it.
3) If you need the SOC 2 Type II full report, we can share it under NDA — I can start the process once procurement confirms.

Timeline: We can return a completed questionnaire within 2 business days and initiate the NDA for SOC 2 access the same day.

Let me know if that works and who the best contact is for procurement/security.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0147

Hi Marissa — thanks for the quick reply. Two items from procurement: 

1) Please populate our vendor security questionnaire (attached) and return by Thursday (2026-07-24). We've attached our standard questionnaire; if you prefer, we can accept your version but we need your answers in our template.
2) We will require SOC 2 Type II (full report) under NDA prior to SOW signature. Please send the NDA link/DocuSign and a point of contact for secure report delivery.

Also confirm whether data export (backup/replication) to the US occurs by default for EU-region customers or if it can be disabled. That will be a gating compliance question for us.

Thanks,

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-22T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: EU Data Residency & Export Controls — Next Steps

Hi everyone — Rafael from Redwood security here. Quick answers and commitments: 

- Vendor questionnaire: we'll complete Acme's template. Marissa, I'll run point on technical responses; Neha will handle contractual items (DPA/BAA).
- SOC 2 Type II: confirmed — we can share the full report under NDA. Marissa, I'll kick off secure delivery and provide the DocuSign/NDA link by EOD tomorrow.
- Replication/export: For hosted EU-region customers, backups are stored in the EU by default. Cross-border replication to non-EU regions is opt-in and subject to contractual controls; we can disable cross-border export for your account.
- OFAC/ITAR: Redwood is not ITAR-controlled. For OFAC, we screen and block sanctioned entities; if you have specific regulatory constraints, share them and we'll map controls.

Action items: 
- Rafael: complete questionnaire and return to procurement by 2026-07-24.
- Marissa: send NDA/DocuSign link to Procurement for SOC 2 access.
- Procurement: confirm any additional export control clauses to include in the SOW.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
